body_ar: لقد اهتمت الشريعة الإسلامية بتطهير النفوس وتزكيتها، ولا تكون تزكية النفوس إلا بالتحلية بالإيمان والقربات ومحاسن الأخلاق، والتخلية من المعاصي والذنوب والأخلاق الرذيلة، ولأهل العلم في هذا الباب تفصيلات تربوية يحتاجها كل مسلم يريد الوصول إلى مقامات اليقين. عناصر تركيب الإنسان وعلاقتها بمراتب الدين: بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم الحمد لله رب العالمين، وأصلي وأسلم على من بعث رحمة للعالمين، وعلى آله وأصحابه ومن اهتدى بهديه واستن بسنته إلى يوم الدين. أما بعد: فإن الله سبحانه وتعالى خلق الإنسان وألفه من ثلاثة عناصر: أشرفها الروح، التي هي نفخة غيبية من أمر الله: وَيَسْأَلُونَكَ عَنِ الرُّوحِ قُلِ الرُّوحُ مِنْ أَمْرِ رَبِّي وَمَا أُوتِيتُمْ مِنَ الْعِلْمِ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا [الإسراء:85]..
body_en:
*[Site synopsis]* The Islamic Sharia has given its attention to the cleansing and purification of souls. The purification of souls comes about only through adorning oneself with faith, with acts that draw one near to God, and with the good qualities of character; and through emptying oneself of acts of disobedience, of sins, and of base qualities. The people of knowledge have, in this field, formative details of which every Muslim stands in need who wishes to reach the stations of certainty.

## The elements of the human being's composition, and their relation to the degrees of the religion

In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Mercy-Giving. Praise belongs to God, Lord of the worlds. I ask God's blessing and peace upon the one sent as a mercy to the worlds, and upon his family and his Companions, and upon all who have taken guidance from his guidance and followed his practice until the Day of Judgement. To proceed:

God, glorified and exalted is He, created the human being and composed him of three elements, the noblest of which is the spirit, which is an unseen breath from God's command: {And they ask you about the spirit. Say: the spirit is of my Lord's command, and you have been given only a little of knowledge.} [al-Isrāʾ 85]..

flags.arabic: خلق الإنسان وألفه من ثلاثة عناصر: أشرفها الروح ... [الإسراء:85]..
flags.context: the last sentence of the record
options: render the first element and the source's own ellipsis, and supply neither of the other two
flags.note: CRITICAL for display. The lesson announces that the human being is composed of three elements, names the first, and breaks off. The other two are never given, and the heading's second half — how the elements relate to the degrees of the religion — is never reached at all. The English supplies nothing. Note that record 658 in this slice reports the Sheikh, at second hand, naming three capacities as spirit, body and intellect; that is a different record about a different lecture and must NOT be used to complete this one.

flags.note: Excerpt only, style guide section 9. It breaks off immediately after naming the first of three announced elements. The complete text sits behind /medias/doc/c-a-16.doc. The English ends exactly where the Arabic ends and completes nothing. Must not be rendered as a whole lesson.

flags.note: The record has two authors. The first paragraph is a synopsis written by the site — it speaks about the lesson and its subject in the third person and does not begin with the opening formula. Everything from the section heading onward is transcribed speech in the Sheikh's own voice. The site must not present the synopsis as his words.

flags.context: the paired terms in the site's synopsis
options: adorning oneself with / emptying oneself of
flags.note: A fixed pair in the literature of spiritual formation — emptying the self of vices and then adorning it with virtues — and in Arabic the two words differ by a single letter, which is much of their force. The wordplay cannot be carried into English; the sense has been kept and the pairing made visible by using parallel constructions. Note that the synopsis gives them in the reverse of the usual order.

flags.context: the goal named at the end of the synopsis
flags.note: 'maqāmāt' is a technical term of the literature of spiritual wayfaring, and 'stations' is its established English rendering. It is the site's word, not the Sheikh's, and it is not in the glossary. Flagged because it places this record in a particular literature and a reviewer may wish the English to be more or less marked accordingly.

translator_notes: One of a run of thirteen records, IDs 688-700, all uploaded on 5 and 8-9 May 2011 within a few hours of one another, all built to the same template and all excerpts. Each carries a site-written synopsis, then a section heading, then the opening formula and first lines of a lesson, and then breaks off; the full text sits behind a .doc download in the /medias/doc/c-a-* series. The uniform timestamps are a bulk upload and say nothing about when the lessons were delivered.

The record contains two distinct voices and the English keeps them apart. The opening paragraph is a synopsis written by the site, about the lesson and in the third person; everything from the section heading onward is the Sheikh's own words as transcribed. Nothing in the synopsis may be quoted as his.
The Qur'anic rendering is interpretive and is not a substitute for the Arabic; the source's own bracket reference style has been kept.
No ruling term appears anywhere in the record.
